scope: 32 original Windows-catalog display overlays; 16 previously enriched plus 16 newly enriched. Immutable original research objects are preserved by the catalog builder.
method: Reviewed official product, repository, license and usage documents. Public package HEAD responses establish anonymous no-charge distribution only for observed main application packages. Revo official portable archive was retrieved solely to read its embedded license; no software was installed or executed.
recommendation_basis: Conditional editorial recommendations and practical tradeoffs inferred from cited documented capabilities. No comparative benchmark, restoration trial, malware test or compatibility installation was performed.
notable_decisions: Process Explorer and Process Monitor current official client requirements are Windows 11 or newer. System Informer current download page/repository list Windows 10/11; an older hosted readme still says Windows 7, so it was used only for plugin limitations, not current platform support.
Sysinternals proprietary license classification is independent of no-charge binary distribution. Seven actual official ZIP HEAD responses support free distribution.
Kopia, Syncthing and rclone free pricing was established using current maintainer application packages rather than inferred from source licensing.
KeePassXC current COPYING identifies GPL-2.0-or-GPL-3.0 and open-source component licenses; its previous generic mixed-license display was corrected.

Everything vendor download page links a MIT-style license for the binary. Full application source availability was not established in this review, so license_kind is conservatively unknown rather than inferred open source from that text.
CrystalDiskInfo current MIT license and November 2026 release are verified; apparent binary HEAD URLs returned HTML interstitials, so pricing remains unknown in this overlay.
BCUninstaller current README explicitly requests maintainers; maintenance remains unverified with that capacity caveat.

Process Lasso official deployment documentation requires commercial purchase within 30 days. The general EULA wording differs in emphasis; the record links both and does not promise unrestricted commercial free use.
Windows-only scope is retained for the Sysinternals Windows binaries; separately linked Linux implementations are not silently assigned the Windows proprietary license.
